title: Double transpose of tensor-counit maps for composite adjunctions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y,\mathcal C_Z$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category], and let $S_f:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_X$ and $S_g:\mathcal C_Z\to\mathcal C_Y$ be strong monoidal functors [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Let $P_f:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$ and $P_g:\mathcal C_Y\to\mathcal C_Z$ have right adjoints $G_f,G_g$, with specified adjunction Hom bijections and counits $\epsilon_f:P_fG_f\to\mathrm{id}$ and $\epsilon_g:P_gG_g\to\mathrm{id}$. Use their composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Suppose $P_f$ has a projection formula relative to $S_f$ and $P_g$ one relative to $S_g$, meaning natural isomorphisms with the unit and associativity equations of [def-sfb-projection-formula], written
$$\pi^f_{B,M}:P_f(S_fB\otimes M)\xrightarrow{\sim}B\otimes P_fM,\qquad
\pi^g_{K,L}:P_g(S_gK\otimes L)\xrightarrow{\sim}K\otimes P_gL.$$
All following expressions use the specified associators, unitors and strong monoidal comparisons. Give $P_c=P_gP_f$ relative to $S_c=S_fS_g$ the composite projection isomorphism
$$\pi^c_{K,M}=\pi^g_{K,P_fM}\circ P_g(\pi^f_{S_gK,M}),$$
and put $G_c=G_fG_g$, with counit $\epsilon^c_K=\epsilon_{g,K}\circ P_g(\epsilon_{f,G_gK})$.
For $h=f,g,c$ define $W_h=G_h\mathbf1$ and $\tau^h_B:S_hB\otimes W_h\to G_hB$ as the adjoint transpose of
$$P_h(S_hB\otimes W_h)\xrightarrow{\pi^h_{B,W_h}}B\otimes P_hW_h
\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{h,\mathbf1}}B\otimes\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\rho_B}B.$$
Write $W=W_f$, $V=W_g$, and $q=\tau^f_V:S_fV\otimes W\to G_fV=W_c$. For any $K\in\mathcal C_Z$ let $N=S_f(S_gK\otimes V)\otimes W$, identified with $S_cK\otimes S_fV\otimes W$. Under
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_X}(N,G_fG_gK)\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_Z}(P_gP_fN,K),$$
both morphisms
$$\tau^f_{G_gK}\circ(S_f\tau^g_K\otimes1_W),\qquad
\tau^c_K\circ(1_{S_cK}\otimes q)$$
have the same inverse transpose, namely
$$\begin{aligned}
P_gP_fN&\xrightarrow{P_g\pi^f_{S_gK\otimes V,W}}
P_g((S_gK\otimes V)\otimes P_fW)\\
&\xrightarrow{P_g(1\otimes\epsilon_{f,\mathbf1})}P_g(S_gK\otimes V)
\xrightarrow{\pi^g_{K,V}}K\otimes P_gV
\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{g,\mathbf1}}K.
\end{aligned}$$
The unit constraints are inserted in the last and second arrows. No $\tau^h$, $q$ or $W_h$ is assumed invertible, and no geometric morphism, smoothness or purity assertion is part of this statement.
The same formula holds for functors and adjunction Hom bijections restricted to full domains of definition, provided all the displayed objects, arrows, Hom bijections and the naturality and projection-coherence equations used in the two composites are defined and hold on those domains. No value outside these domains is asserted.
